title: The Package That Took a Different Route
title_ja: 別の経路をたどった荷物
fact_notes: オリジナル教材。架空の例を用いた論説であり、実在の調査・史料・制度・実証結果ではない。制作台帳は来歴確認用。

sentences.en: When people order goods from another country, the delivery process may appear to begin at a shop and end at a customer's door.
sentences.ja: 他国から品物を注文すると、配送過程は店で始まり客の玄関で終わるように見えるかもしれない。

sentences.en: Between these two points, however, the package may pass through several organizations whose activities must be coordinated across geographical and administrative boundaries.
sentences.ja: しかしその二点間で荷物は地理的・行政的境界を越えて活動を調整する必要がある複数の組織を通過する可能性がある。

sentences.en: A delay at one location can affect arrangements made by people who have never directly communicated with one another.
sentences.ja: ある地点の遅延は直接意思疎通したことのない人々の手配に影響し得る。

sentences.en: An imaginary example helps illustrate this less visible aspect of international trade.
sentences.ja: 架空の例は国際貿易の見えにくい側面を示す助けになる。

sentences.en: A small company sends a collection of handmade products to a shop overseas.
sentences.ja: 小企業が手作り製品を海外の店に送る。

sentences.en: The shipment is expected to arrive before an exhibition, but an unexpected interruption prevents it from following its original route.
sentences.ja: 展示前の到着が予定されているが予期しない中断が当初経路をたどるのを妨げる。

sentences.en: A transport company identifies an alternative connection that could deliver the goods later than originally planned, but still before the exhibition begins.
sentences.ja: 運送会社は当初予定より遅いが展示開始前に配送できる代替接続を特定する。

sentences.en: The shop nevertheless needs to receive reliable information about the revised schedule before deciding whether to change its preparations.
sentences.ja: それでも店は準備を変えるか決める前に修正日程について信頼できる情報を受け取る必要がある。

sentences.en: The manufacturer, transport company, and shop each possess information that the other participants may need.
sentences.ja: 製造業者、運送会社、店は互いに必要とするかもしれない情報をそれぞれ持っている。

sentences.en: For example, the shop knows the latest time at which the goods could usefully arrive, while the transport company understands the limitations of the available routes.
sentences.ja: 例えば店は荷物が有用な形で到着できる最も遅い時刻を知り、運送会社は利用可能経路の限界を理解する。

sentences.en: An announcement containing only the word delayed would not necessarily allow either organization to make an informed decision.
sentences.ja: 遅延という語だけを含む通知ではどちらの組織も十分な情報に基づく判断ができるとは限らない。

sentences.en: Effective coordination requires information about both the change and the consequences that matter to the people receiving it.
sentences.ja: 効果的な調整には変化と受け手に重要な影響の両方について情報が必要だ。

sentences.en: The fictional case does not provide a guide to actual shipping regulations or establish which transport method would be best.
sentences.ja: 架空例は実際の輸送規制の手引きでも最適輸送法の確定でもない。

sentences.en: Instead, it illustrates how uncertainty about one part of a process can create difficulties elsewhere, even when each participant performs an assigned task responsibly.
sentences.ja: 代わりに各参加者が割り当てられた作業を責任をもって行っても過程の一部の不確実性が別の場所で困難を生む様子を示す。

sentences.en: The organizations need to understand which decisions depend on information that others are capable of providing.
sentences.ja: 組織はどの判断が他者の提供可能な情報に依存するか理解する必要がある。

sentences.en: Without that understanding, a technically successful delivery may nevertheless fail to serve its intended purpose.
sentences.ja: その理解がなければ技術的に成功した配送も目的を果たせない場合がある。

sentences.en: International cooperation often depends on the coordination of decisions made in different places and under different constraints.
sentences.ja: 国際協力は異なる場所・制約下で行われる判断の調整に依存する場合が多い。

sentences.en: A network is valuable not only because it allows goods to move but also because it connects people who must adapt their plans when circumstances change.
sentences.ja: ネットワークは物資移動を可能にするだけでなく事情が変わると計画を調整する必要のある人々を結ぶので価値がある。

sentences.en: Recognizing those relationships helps explain why reliable communication is an essential component of trade.
sentences.ja: その関係を認識すると信頼できる意思疎通が貿易の不可欠要素である理由を説明できる。

sentences.en: The journey of a package is consequently a story about information as well as transportation.
sentences.ja: 荷物の旅はしたがって輸送だけでなく情報についての物語である。

vocabulary.definition: in or relating to another country
act of arranging things to work together

questions.prompt: Why is international delivery more complex than it appears?
options: Every package travels through the same organization.
Customers always communicate directly with all workers.
It involves multiple organizations coordinating across boundaries.
Delivery begins only after goods reach a customer.

questions.prompt: What can a delay at one place affect?
options: Only the shape of the package.
The shop's decision to close permanently.
An unexpected disruption to its planned route.

questions.prompt: Why does the shop need the revised schedule?
options: It must determine how the products were made.
It has already canceled the exhibition.
It wants to select a different manufacturer.
Its preparations depend on when the goods will arrive.
questions.explanation_ja: 到着時期に準備が依存する。

questions.prompt: What information does the shop possess?
Why is the word delayed insufficient?
options: It does not describe the timing or consequences needed for decisions.
Every delay has an identical duration.
A delay cannot be communicated in words.
A short announcement always gives all relevant information.
questions.explanation_ja: 判断に必要な情報が不足する。

questions.prompt: What might happen even if each participant works responsibly?
options: Participants no longer need to communicate.
A lack of information about dependencies can cause problems elsewhere.

questions.prompt: What does the case not establish?
options: The role of an intended purpose.
questions.explanation_ja: 実際の最適輸送法は未確定。

options: Each participant should plan without information from others.
International trade requires coordinating relevant information as well as moving goods.
Shipping is useful only when no delays ever occur.
questions.explanation_ja: 輸送と情報調整の両方が重要。

grammar.explanation_ja: whoseは所有格の関係代名詞。
before＋動名詞、whether to doは〜するか。

grammar.focus: not only because it allows goods to move but also because
grammar.explanation_ja: not only A but also Bで理由を並列。

paraphrases.source: Between these two points, however, the package may pass through several organizations whose activities must be coordinated across geographical and administrative boundaries.
paraphrases.rewrite: The package passes through organizations that must coordinate their work.

paraphrases.source: The shop nevertheless needs to receive reliable information about the revised schedule before deciding whether to change its preparations.
paraphrases.rewrite: The shop needs the revised schedule in order to decide if changes are necessary.

paraphrases.source: For example, the shop knows the latest time at which the goods could usefully arrive, while the transport company understands the limitations of the available routes.
paraphrases.rewrite: The shop knows its deadline, whereas the carrier knows the available routes.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 各組織が持つ情報の差。

paraphrases.source: A network is valuable not only because it allows goods to move but also because it connects people who must adapt their plans when circumstances change.
paraphrases.rewrite: A network enables both transportation and coordination among people.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: ネットワークの二つの価値。

discourse.role_ja: 単純な配送の印象と複雑さ。
代替経路があっても情報が必要。
各組織が持つ情報の具体例。
実際の輸送助言でなく概念の説明。

cloze.explanation_ja: 過程の一部の不確実性。
